scenarios.name: SEO 301 redirects: resolve + middleware degrade-open
scenarios.description: PallasTrade::Redirect maps per-store from_path → to_path (normalized: leading slash, strip trailing slash; from_path strips pasted origin; to_path must be internal). Redirects carry optional business-facing title/description (columns added 2026-08-15) so the admin list is readable (Title column first, position 5); Admin API permitted_params and admin redirect_serializer both expose title/description. Store API resolve returns {path, status_code} or null; storefront middleware issues NextResponse.redirect guarded against A→A loops and degrades OPEN on API failure (Turnstile-style). Admin API /api/v3/admin/redirects is full CRUD behind read/write_settings. Admin pages must carry plain-language explainer copy (page_alerts intro on index, form_intro on new/edit via shared _form) so non-technical users understand the feature (old link → new link, prevent 404, keep SEO rank). The redirects index also shows a 'Products with changed URLs' list (from friendly_id `friendly_id_slugs` history via PallasTrade::ProductUrlChange — old slug ≠ current, excludes deleted- slugs and already-handled from_paths) with one-click links that pre-fill /admin/redirects/new?from_path=/products/{old}&to_path=/products/{new} (RedirectsController#new reads those query params). Next.js 16: the 301 resolution lives in src/lib/pallastrade/middleware.ts (createPallasTradeMiddleware) wired via src/proxy.ts — do NOT add a separate src/middleware.ts (Next 16 rejects middleware + proxy coexistence). Storefront must pass pnpm check (Biome) before commit — new image/srcset paths use plain with CDN webp variants, not the Next.js optimizer.
mustDo: Normalize paths on save (leading slash, no trailing slash; from_path origin-strip; to_path internal-only)
Enforce unique from_path per store; active scope ignored in resolve
Resolve endpoint returns target + status on hit, data:null on miss
Storefront middleware 301s on hit with loop guard and 60s revalidate cache
Degrade open (continue rendering) when the resolve API is unreachable
List products whose URL changed (friendly_id_slugs history via PallasTrade::ProductUrlChange) on /admin/redirects with one-click redirect creation (prefilled from_path/to_path)
mustNotDo: Allow external URLs as to_path (open-redirect)
Redirect A → A (loop)

Run CDN webp variants through the Next.js optimizer again (double encoding)

scenarios.name: Back-in-stock notifications: guest subscribe + event-driven email
scenarios.description: PallasTrade::BackInStockSubscription (core model, table pallastrade_back_in_stock_subscriptions, store+product+email+status default 'active', unique [product_id,email]) is the single source of truth. Customers subscribe on an out-of-stock product through the Store API POST /api/v3/store/products/:product_id/back_in_stock_subscriptions (guest-accessible, rate-limited; body {email}, normalized/downcased; find_or_initialize_by(product,email) re-activates a previously-notified subscription; 404 when product missing). Storefront renders BackInStockNotify on ProductDetails when the variant is out of stock (sdk.backInStockSubscriptions.create, success/error states). PallasTrade::BackInStockSubscriber (registered in core engine subscribers) listens to product.back_in_stock (published by StockMovement::CustomEvents) and emails each active BackInStockSubscription via PallasTrade::BackInStockMailer (BaseMailer + with_store_locale, HTML+text, product URL from store.url/default_country), then marks each notified (idempotent). Email delivery uses the store's configured SMTP (Resend: smtp.resend.com / SMTP_USERNAME=resend / SMTP_PASSWORD=re_... in server .env only). Admin lists/deletes subscriptions at /admin/back_in_stock_subscriptions (settings nav, table with product/email/status/created_at).
mustDo: Guest can subscribe with just an email on an out-of-stock product (Store API, no auth)
Idempotent per (product, email); re-subscribing a notified subscription reactivates it
product.back_in_stock event emails every active subscription then marks them notified (no duplicate emails)
Emails render in store locale with correct product URL; use BaseMailer + with_store_locale
Admin can list and delete subscriptions
SMTP credentials (Resend API key) live only in the server .env, never committed
mustNotDo: Expose raw integer primary keys in API responses
Send duplicate emails to an already-notified subscription
Publish product.back_in_stock without a real out-of-stock → in-stock transition
Commit Resend/SMTP secrets to source

scenarios.name: Storefront bugfix after rollback to 2155920: average_rating Number guard + checkout hydration (mounted gate + NEXT_PUBLIC_* build/runtime divergence + Stripe key baking)
scenarios.description: After rolling back to 2155920 (no order-split/combined-payment), three regressions resurfaced: (1) the PDP crashed with `TypeError: b?.toFixed is not a function` because ProductReviews rendered `averageRating?.toFixed(1)` while the Store API serializes average_rating as a string (BigDecimal) — fixed by wrapping in Number(). (2) checkout rendered blank / stuck skeleton (React #418 hydration mismatch). Root cause: NEXT_PUBLIC_STORE_NAME=PallasTrade-Dev existed only in the runtime env file while the client bundle was built without it (client inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time, server reads runtime env) — fixed by baking NEXT_PUBLIC_STORE_NAME/SITE_URL/DEFAULT_LOCALE/DEFAULT_COUNTRY as Docker build args (storefront/Dockerfile + deploy.yml + docker-compose.dev.yml) so server and client render the same strings; the mounted gate (SSR skeleton until client mount) is the fallback. (3) the Stripe PaymentElement rendered an EMPTY container on checkout — the rollback dropped the original b68095f Dockerfile `ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` declaration, so the build arg was silently ignored, the client bundle shipped without the publishable key, stripePromise resolved to null, and Elements rendered nothing (backend still created PaymentIntents 201). Fixed by restoring the ARG/ENV + build-arg in Dockerfile/deploy.yml/compose.
